name: MC33063ADR2G
title: 1.5 A step-up, step-down and inverting DC-DC converter control circuit
summary: A bipolar DC-DC converter controller with its own 1.5 A output switch, made in four grades: MC34063A, MC33063A, SC33063A and NCV33063A. One chip holds a temperature-compensated 1.25 V reference, a comparator, an oscillator whose duty cycle is controlled and which carries a peak-current limit, a driver transistor and a Darlington-capable output switch. With a few outside parts it makes a step-up, step-down or voltage-inverting converter from 3.0 to 40 V in, at up to 100 kHz, with the output set by two resistors. The grades differ in ambient range (0 to +70 °C, -40 to +85 °C, or -40 to +125 °C); the NCV part is AEC-Q100 qualified.
key_figures: up to 100 kHz; 33 kHz typ at CT = 1.0 nF
4.0 mA max, VCC = 5.0 V to 40 V, CT = 1.0 nF

notes: Package suffix: D is SOIC-8 (case 751), P or P1 is PDIP-8 (case 626); G is Pb-free. A V after the A marks the -40 to +125 °C grade.

Marking: the SOIC top line is 3x063 (3x063V for the V grade), the PDIP top line 3x063AP1 or 33063AVP, with x = 3 or 4 by family. The lines below carry assembly site, wafer lot, year, work week and the Pb-free mark.
NCV33063A: Tlow = −40 °C, Thigh = +125 °C, guaranteed by design. The NCV prefix is for automotive and other uses that need site and change control; it is AEC-Q100 qualified and PPAP capable.
All parts are Pb-free, halogen free / BFR free and RoHS compliant.

circuits.title: Step-up converter, 12 V in, 28 V at 175 mA out
circuits.description: A boost converter. The 170 µH inductor runs from the sensed supply node to the switch collector; when the switch opens, the 1N5819 carries the inductor current into the 330 output capacitor. The switch emitter is grounded and the driver collector is fed through 180 Ω from the sensed supply node. Rsc = 0.22 Ω between Vin and pin 7 sets the peak current limit; 1500 pF on pin 3 sets the oscillator. R2 = 47 k and R1 = 2.2 k feed the output back to pin 5: 1.25 × (1 + 47/2.2) ≈ 28 V. A 1.0 µH and 100 LC stage after the output is an optional filter that brings the ripple down.

parts.note: 38 turns of #22 AWG on a 55117 toroid

notes: Line regulation 30 mV (±0.05 %) for Vin = 8.0 to 16 V; efficiency 87.7 % at 12 V and 175 mA; ripple 400 mVpp, 40 mVpp with the optional filter.

circuits.title: Step-down converter, 25 V in, 5.0 V at 500 mA out
circuits.description: A buck converter. Driver and switch collectors (pins 8 and 1) both tie to the sensed supply node, so the two transistors work as a Darlington and the switch emitter drives the 220 µH inductor. The 1N5819 from ground to the switch emitter carries the inductor current while the switch is off. Rsc = 0.33 Ω sets the current limit and 470 pF on pin 3 the oscillator. R2 = 3.6 k over R1 = 1.2 k gives 1.25 × (1 + 3.6/1.2) = 5.0 V. The 470 output capacitor holds the output, and a 1.0 µH / 100 LC stage is an optional ripple filter.

parts.note: 48 turns of #22 AWG on a 55117 toroid

notes: Short-circuit current 1.1 A at Vin = 25 V into 0.1 Ω; efficiency 83.7 % at 25 V and 500 mA; ripple 120 mVpp, 40 mVpp with the optional filter.

circuits.title: Voltage inverting converter, 4.5 to 6.0 V in, −12 V at 100 mA out
circuits.description: An inverting buck-boost. Pins 8 and 1 tie to the sensed supply node (Darlington), and the switch emitter drives the 88 µH inductor whose other end is grounded. When the switch opens, the inductor pulls current up from the output through the 1N5819, charging the 1000 µF output capacitor negative. The chip's GND pin and the timing capacitor return to the −12 V output, so the comparator works relative to it: R1 = 953 Ω from pin 5 to the output and R2 = 8.2 k from pin 5 to ground give |Vout| = 1.25 × (1 + 8200/953) ≈ 12 V. Rsc = 0.24 Ω sets the current limit; a 1.0 µH / 100 LC stage is an optional ripple filter.

parts.note: 28 turns of #22 AWG on a 55117 toroid
optional output filter; polarised, + to ground

notes: Short-circuit current 910 mA at Vin = 5.0 V into 0.1 Ω; efficiency 62.2 % at 5.0 V and 100 mA; ripple 500 mVpp, 70 mVpp with the optional filter.

circuits.title: Step-up with an external NPN switch, for peak current above 1.5 A
circuits.description: The boost converter with an outside NPN carrying the inductor current. The on-chip switch emitter drives the NPN's base, with a resistor from base to ground; the chip's switch collector joins the NPN collector at the inductor and diode.
notes: Pins 3, 4 and 5 connect as in the basic converter of the same kind.

circuits.title: Step-up with an external saturated NPN switch, for peak current above 1.5 A
circuits.description: As the external-NPN boost, but the inductor is tapped: the chip's switch collector reaches the tap through a resistor R, while the outside NPN collector and the diode sit on the inductor's far end, so the outside NPN is driven into saturation. R goes toward 0 when Vin is constant. The note on hard saturation (up to 2.0 µs to recover) applies.

parts.note: from the inductor tap to pin 1; R → 0 for constant Vin
tapped inductor; pins 1 and 2 are the ends, T the tap

notes: Pins 3, 4 and 5 connect as in the basic converter of the same kind.

circuits.title: Step-down with an external NPN switch, for peak current above 1.5 A
circuits.description: The buck converter with an outside NPN switch. Pins 8 and 1 and the NPN collector tie to the sensed supply node; the chip's switch emitter drives the NPN base, with a resistor from base to ground. The NPN emitter feeds the inductor and the catch diode.
notes: Pins 3, 4 and 5 connect as in the basic converter of the same kind.

circuits.title: Step-down with an external saturated PNP switch, for peak current above 1.5 A
circuits.description: The buck converter with an outside PNP as a saturated high-side switch. Its emitter sits on the sensed supply node with a resistor from emitter to base; the joined driver and switch collectors (pins 8 and 1) pull the base down through a series resistor. The switch emitter is grounded. The PNP collector feeds the inductor and the catch diode.
notes: Pins 3, 4 and 5 connect as in the basic converter of the same kind.

circuits.title: Voltage inverting with an external NPN switch, for peak current above 1.5 A
circuits.description: The inverting converter with an outside NPN switch. Pins 8 and 1 and the NPN collector tie to the sensed supply node; the switch emitter drives the NPN base, with a resistor from base to ground. The NPN emitter drives the grounded inductor, and the diode carries current from the negative output to it. The chip's GND pin and the timing capacitor return to the output.
notes: Pin 5 connects as in the basic inverting converter.

circuits.title: Voltage inverting with an external saturated PNP switch, for peak current above 1.5 A
circuits.description: The inverting converter with an outside PNP as saturated switch. Its emitter sits on the sensed supply node with a resistor from emitter to base; the joined pins 8 and 1 pull the base through a series resistor. The PNP collector drives the grounded inductor and the diode from the output. The chip's switch emitter, GND pin and timing capacitor all return to the negative output.
notes: Pin 5 connects as in the basic inverting converter.

operation.text: The die holds a 1.25 V temperature-compensated reference regulator, a comparator, an oscillator with peak-current (Ipk) sensing, a gate and set-reset latch, a driver transistor Q2 and an output switch Q1, with a 100 Ω resistor from Q1's base to its emitter. The comparator's non-inverting input takes the reference and its inverting input is pin 5. It uses 79 active transistors.

The timing capacitor on pin 3 is charged by about 35 µA and discharged by about 220 µA, a discharge-to-charge ratio of 6.5 typ. With 1.0 nF the frequency is 33 kHz typ (24 to 42 kHz). The pin 3 voltage is a sawtooth; at VCC = 5 V and 1.0 nF it runs between about 0.43 V and 1.26 V with a period near 28.6 µs (35 kHz). The part works up to 100 kHz.

Rsc between VCC (pin 6) and Ipk Sense (pin 7) carries the switch current. When its drop reaches the sense voltage, 300 mV typ (250 to 350 mV) at 25 °C, the peak switch current is limited; Rsc = 0.3 / Ipk(switch). The sense voltage falls with temperature, from about 309 mV at −55 °C to about 248 mV at 125 °C.

With pins 1 and 8 joined, Q2 and Q1 form a Darlington: saturation voltage 1.0 V typ, 1.3 V max at 1.0 A, and the switch never saturates. With pin 8 fed through its own resistor (82 Ω to VCC for a forced β near 20), Q1 saturates to 0.45 V typ, 0.7 V max at 1.0 A, but can take up to 2.0 µs to turn off at switch currents of 300 mA or less with 30 mA or more of driver current, which shortens the off time at 30 kHz and above, worst when hot. The forced β is then to be 10 or more, counting that Q2's 100 Ω emitter resistor takes about 7.0 mA before Q1 conducts.

For peak currents over 1.5 A an outside transistor carries the inductor current: an NPN whose base is driven from the switch emitter, or a saturated switch: an NPN for the step-up, a PNP for the step-down and the inverter. Each converter kind has both forms.

The design starts from the nominal input voltage Vin, the output voltage, the output current Iout, the lowest switching frequency fmin at the chosen Vin and IO, and the peak-to-peak ripple Vripple(pp). From these the formulas give ton/toff, the timing capacitor, peak switch current, Rsc, the least inductance and the output capacitor. The output capacitor from the formula is a lower bound: its ESR and the board layout call for more.

The example converters use toroids wound on a Magnetics Inc. 55117 core with #22 AWG wire: 170 µH (38 turns) for the step-up, 220 µH (48 turns) for the step-down and 88 µH (28 turns) for the inverter.

With the switch off (pin 5 above threshold), CT = 1.0 nF, the chip draws 4.0 mA max from 5.0 to 40 V. Typically the standby current rises steeply to about 3.1 mA by VCC ≈ 4 V, then slowly to about 3.4 mA at 40 V.

MC34063A runs from 0 to +70 °C ambient; MC33063A and SC33063A from −40 to +85 °C; MC33063AV and NCV33063A from −40 to +125 °C. The V grades allow 6.0 mV max threshold line regulation against 5.0 mV for the others. The NCV33063A serves automotive and other uses needing site and change control, AEC-Q100 qualified and PPAP capable.
